audit.why: Nautilus at 1, Akali from 2-3 and again from first item, level with him at 4-6, matches 49.87% Emerald+ over 24 games and both on-disk charts. 24 games is far too small to move a chart on, so nothing was touched.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes read 'Dredge Line online, level 6, first item' with no numbers, and gave Akali 'levels 2-3'.
audit.why: Twilight Shroud is not learnable before level 3. His level-6 spike is Depth Charge on 120/100/80s from 825 range - and unlike Dredge Line it needs no aim, which is the reason his 6 is dangerous and his 1-5 is dodgeable.
audit.corrected: breakdown.spikes, phases[0].why and phases[4].why rebuilt on level 3, the 14s Dredge Line and the 120s Depth Charge.

audit.whatIsWrong: Titan's Wrath appears nowhere in either layer, and the content layer twice says Twilight Shroud refunds energy.
audit.why: Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield that also makes his attacks burn you and everything near you - it is the single reason a clean Akali opener fails on him, and the _missing file flags this matchup shield-absorbs-burst on exactly that ability. Separately, Riot's text for Twilight Shroud gives move speed and nothing else; it costs 0 energy and refunds none, so 'the energy and move speed it refunds' was inventing a resource swing.
audit.corrected: tldr, report[0].t, report[5].t, dontsFull[1], report[11].t, breakdown.cooldowns and content whys[3], mid and wants.you[2] now carry the 12s shield, and the energy-refund claim is deleted.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns said only 'His only engage. Shroud-dodge it.'
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s from 1150 range - a genuinely long cooldown on a single skillshot, which is precisely why sidestepping it wins the lane. Riptide is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s and Depth Charge 120/100/80s.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, winCon, report[1].t and report[9].t now state them.

edits.before: Around 4-5 your Shroud (W) starts paying off — drop it the instant he commits a hook so it breaks his targeting and reset the trade with the energy and move speed it refunds. At 6 the lane swings to you: Perfect Execution (R) gives you a gap-closer and a missing-health execute, so any time his Q is down you can E-mark in, R-through, and burst him before his tank items exist. Just respect that a landed hook plus Riptide and the passive root can still chain you if you dive in with no energy and Shroud on cooldown.
edits.after: Around 4-5 your Shroud (W) starts paying off — drop it the instant he commits a hook so it breaks his targeting and reset the trade with the move speed it grants. At 6 the lane swings to you: Perfect Execution (R) gives you a gap-closer and a missing-health execute, so any time his Q is down you can E-mark in, R-through, and burst him before his tank items exist. Just respect Titan's Wrath — that flat 12s shield eats your opener, and a landed hook into Riptide and the passive root still chains you if you dive with Shroud down.

notes: The 'Twilight Shroud refunds energy' claim appeared twice in this entry. Twilight Shroud costs 0 energy and Riot's text grants only move speed, so the same phrasing is worth grepping for across the rest of the Akali content file — it reads like a shared template line rather than a one-off.
